marta: Quick heads-up — I’m scheduling a tf apply for control-plane routing rewrite during the release window tonight 00:30-01:30 UTC. Canary will be us-west-2 subnet-3, then stagger to remaining subnets if green. Please ack if you have any objections or need a pin.
deploybot: [deploybot] queued: terraform plan for infra/networking (branch=release/2026-03-routing). Plan id: pb-4421. No changes to production secrets. Change summary: update route table attachments, add new egress gateway, modify iam binding for infra-deploy-sa.
marta: Important notes — provider pinned in modules/networking to hash v1.7.2 (we pinned last week). Service account rotation included: will add new binding before traffic switch. Operator run command (example):
```
terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config=prod.hcl
terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out=plan.pb
terraform apply -parallelism=8 plan.pb
```
We'll use -parallelism=8 to avoid API throttles. I will not run apply until canary sign-off.
dan: Acked. Two things: 1) Route53 TTLs for the internal endpoints are 60s; good. 2) Need a short drain window for instances with sticky sessions — will coordinate with app owners. Also confirm terraform state lock held by CI worker? Who will be running the apply?
jules: Thanks. I can run the canary apply in us-west-2. I’ll follow the checklist: snapshot, apply, smoke, metrics check (p95, error-rate). If any step fails we rollback route attachments.
marta: @jules perfect. CI will push plan; I’ll hand off to you to run apply. Plan includes an IAM change to add role: arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/infra-deploy-sa -> attach policies: ec2:ModifyNetworkInterfaces, routes:Update. That will require a quick permissions review — @leo please confirm no org-level restrict will block.
leo: Confirmed — policies allowed. Note: we must avoid changing the deploy-sa name; rotation will create infra-deploy-sa-v2 then swap. I’ll watch CloudTrail and approvals. Also ensure vault token TTL is extended for the window.
anita: Can we include an explicit rollback playbook in the thread? Short checklist: 1) Re-attach previous route tables via infra rollback module (terraform apply -target=module.routing -var-file=rollback.tfvars). 2) Rebind old IAM role; 3) Repoint egress gateway; 4) Open ticket and tag release engineers. Add the exact commands here so anyone can run them quickly.
marta: Good call, @anita. Rollback snippet (keeps it minimal):
```
# quick rollback to previous routing state
terraform init -reconfigure
terraform apply -auto-approve -target=module.routing -var-file=rollback.tfvars
# restore iam
terraform apply -auto-approve -target=module.iam -var-file=rollback.tfvars
```
If the apply fails midway, do NOT run a full apply for 5 minutes — check state and SRE logs first.
deploybot: [deploybot] status: canary plan ready. Awaiting manual apply by jules. ETA: 00:42 UTC.
jules: I’ll run canary at 00:42. Quick runbook: 1) snapshot subnet-3 AMIs 2) apply plan 3) run smoke tests (http health, egress path test, host-level metrics) 4) if pass, schedule staggered applies every 6 minutes across AZs.
dan: Reminder: communicate change-window to oncall and PG teams. I posted a short note in #all-hands and pinged app-ops. Also leaving a tag on the provider module for traceability.
marta: Thanks team. If anyone sees a blocker before 00:30 ping here. Otherwise I’ll mark this as "go for canary" in 15m.
leo: +1. Watching logs and quota. If we see API throttle >10% during apply, abort and rollback.
anita: +1 from security. I’ll monitor IAM bindings and run quick audit after swap.
jules: Running canary now — will post results in this thread. :rocket:
